title: sqlite-mcp read-only mode can be bypassed with injected statements
summary: Statement chaining in execute_query and injection in describe_table can bypass the default read-only mode. ATTACH can modify the protected database, read other SQLite files or create SQLite files.

severity.rationale: The flaw undermines read-only access and permits database changes. Its documented effects concern the SQLite service and files accessible to its process.

exposure: An attacker must reach the MCP tools. The server has no built-in authentication and defaults to listening on all interfaces. Existing non-SQLite files are not arbitrarily overwritten.

params.instructions: Check github.com/StacklokLabs/sqlite-mcp version and whether the documented exposure conditions apply.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade to 0.1.2. Until then, restrict access and mount only the intended database read-only at the filesystem or container layer.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm the deployed component uses the patched release and test the affected workflow with harmless inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
